tasks.short: Examine returned parts and arrange exchanges or refunds

steps.what: Examine returned parts for defects and determine the appropriate return outcome
Enter and check the exchange or refund transaction for defective parts
Exchange the returned part or explain the refund and next steps

tasks.design: Configure the till or returns system {OTHER} to reuse the original transaction's item and payment fields. The salesperson examines the part, decides the return outcome and checks the exact transaction before refund or exchange; physical handover and quarantine retain their time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Return entry can repeat original sale details after the condition decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Native original-sale lookup and return forms can reduce repeated entry.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing defects, misuse and uncertain compatibility while applying local return authority.
tasks.human_edge: The salesperson can notice a physical defect or customer concern that a transaction record cannot establish.
tasks.altitude: Less return entry with inspection and customer resolution intact.

reach.task: Match a refund to the checked original payment transaction

evidence.claim: Original-sale lookup can reduce return entry; physical defect inspection and refund authority still require people. This is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is salesperson inspection, return transaction and handover, excluding payment-provider runtime and later supplier warranty recovery.

Salesperson produces item identity, observed defect, return outcome and reason in s1 with all 50 hours retained. s2's 21 retained hours include transaction lookup, field capture, payment and amount checks and authorised release.
No structured defect code is supplied free. Missing purchase evidence or unmatched payment returns to manual checking; no automatic refund is initiated.
Test native returns first; existing prefills earn no new gain. Approval binds exact customer, item, amount, payment destination and action; changes require a renewed check.
unknowns: Current return-entry burden and native functions
research_questions: Can sale reuse shorten return entry without wrong-item, wrong-amount or wrong-payment refunds?

already_counted.description: Return entry, exact transaction checks and release

incremental.description: Maintain return fields and review transaction exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Final customer, original sale, item, quantity, refund amount, payment destination and exchange action; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=50+21+20=91; gross 9 minus 2 upkeep gives net 7. High assumes repeated sale-data entry; low removes only 2 hours, offset by upkeep. Physical inspection and handover retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compare shipping methods, costs and package status

steps.what: Verify shipment address, parcel measurements and delivery requirements
Research shipping methods and compare applicable costs and service conditions
Select and book the agreed shipping method after checking costs
Track packages and investigate delayed or conflicting shipping status

tasks.design: Test a native multi-carrier connector in {OPS_SYSTEM} for current rate comparison and tracking from {PARTNER_PORTAL}. The salesperson verifies parcel inputs, checks service conditions and books the exact selected service; stale rates, excluded goods and ambiguous status return to manual carrier contact.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated carrier lookups can duplicate shipment fields and status polling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native carrier connectors can consolidate rate and tracking retrieval.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete parcel data, surcharges, service exclusions and delivery exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: The salesperson can reject a cheap service that will not meet the customer's actual requirement.
tasks.altitude: Less carrier browsing and status polling with shipment and exception decisions retained.

reach.task: Check a parcel specification before requesting a service quote

evidence.claim: Carrier rate and tracking integrations can reduce repeated lookup when reliable shipment fields exist; the estimate is model knowledge, not a sourced shipping case.

assumptions: Boundary is salesperson shipment management, excluding packing, carrier transport and customer labour.

Salesperson produces recipient, street, number, postcode, country, measured weight and dimensions with units, contents restrictions, declared value and required delivery date in s1; its full 25 hours retain all verification and capture. No ready structured address is assumed.

Carrier produces rate, currency, service, exclusions, surcharge basis and timestamp during existing quotation work. s2 retains 15 hours for checks and missing-field queries. s3 records the tracking identifier; carrier produces status events through existing transport work and s4 retains 10 hours for interpretation and exceptions.
Test native connectors first. Missing coverage or stale data returns to manual lookup. Existing carrier automation earns no labour saving; no automatic customer promise or booking occurs.
unknowns: Carrier connector coverage and current lookup burden
research_questions: Does consolidated lookup reduce total rate and tracking work without hidden surcharges or missed delivery exceptions?

already_counted.description: Shipment measurement, address verification and structured capture
Service checks and manual quote exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain carrier fields, service rules and failed-lookup handling

approvals.approved_version: Exact shipment specification, carrier, service, quoted cost and destination snapshot; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=25+15+20+10=70; gross 30 minus 4 upkeep gives net 26. High requires repeated rate browsing and status polling with connector coverage; low removes only 4 hours in low-volume or exception-heavy work, offset by upkeep. Input capture and booking decisions retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise on part substitutions when identical replacements are unavailable

steps.what: Clarify equipment identity and requirements when identical replacement parts are unavailable
Locate and check candidate substitution parts against verified fitment information
Advise customers on substitution or modification limits and escalate uncertain compatibility

tasks.design: Configure fitment and original-part filters in the parts catalogue {OTHER}, returning source-backed alternatives. The salesperson checks compatibility and availability and explains limitations; modification proposals without documented compatibility require authorised technical confirmation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding documented cross-references can require repeated catalogue searching.
tasks.enabler_now: Native fitment filters can narrow alternatives without a language model making compatibility claims.
tasks.still_hard: Variant differences, safety-critical applications and undocumented modifications.
tasks.human_edge: The salesperson can recognise missing application detail and refuse to promise a fit.
tasks.altitude: Less catalogue searching with compatibility judgement and customer dialogue retained.

reach.task: Capture the equipment and original-part identifiers for technical checking

evidence.claim: Algolia's auto-parts search filters vehicle fitment and suggests alternatives; TecDoc finds parts by VIN, plate or original-equipment number. This supports vehicle catalogue lookup, not arbitrary modification approval.

assumptions: Boundary is replacement advice, excluding engineering approval, physical modification and sales order execution. Vehicle evidence applies only to covered vehicle catalogues.

Salesperson produces equipment or vehicle identifier, model variant, original part number, required function and constraints in s1 with all 30 hours retained. No structured compatibility requirement is supplied free.

Catalogue provider produces fitment, cross-reference and source version through existing licensed data work; no new free supplier work is assumed. s2 retains 18 hours for source checking, candidate review and missing-data queries.

Test native filters before custom matching. Existing lookup capability earns no new gain; missing fitment returns to manual technical checking. No photo guess or inferred modification is accepted as approval.
unknowns: Current lookup burden and technical escalation route
research_questions: Can fitment filtering reduce lookup without recommending incompatible variants or unsupported modifications?

already_counted.description: Requirement capture and equipment identity checks

incremental.description: Maintain catalogue links and audit compatibility exceptions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=30+18+40=88; gross 12 minus 3 upkeep gives net 9. High assumes covered fitment data and repeated cross-reference searches; low removes only 3 hours in poorly covered or complex work, offset by upkeep. Requirements and customer advice retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss part features and appropriate use

steps.what: Locate and verify part features and use information for the equipment
Discuss use and features of parts and clarify customer understanding

tasks.design: Configure source links from the parts catalogue {OTHER} to current manufacturer instructions in {DOCS}. The salesperson verifies the application and explains features and use directly, escalating questions beyond documented instructions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the precise current feature or use passage can interrupt discussion.
tasks.enabler_now: Native item-linked sources can reduce retrieval without generating new technical claims.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining limitations in the customer's actual equipment context and detecting misunderstanding.
tasks.human_edge: The salesperson can recognise an unsafe intended use and clarify it before a sale.
tasks.altitude: Less source hunting; customer explanation retains its time.

reach.task: Find the current instruction source for a specified part

evidence.claim: Native item-linked references can reduce feature lookup while application judgement and explanation remain; this is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is feature and use advice, excluding substitution assessment and sales transactions.

Salesperson clarifies and captures question, equipment identity, part number, instruction version and applicable passage within s1's retained 14 hours. No ready structured customer question is assumed.
Manufacturer produces instructions through existing product documentation work; no new supplier collection is transferred. Missing or conflicting instructions require manual checking and escalation.
Try native links before custom software. Existing source links earn no new gain. All explanation and understanding checks retain their time; overlapping substitution advice is allocated once.
unknowns: Current retrieval burden and source coverage
research_questions: Can source links reduce lookup while preserving warnings and avoiding the wrong part version?

already_counted.description: Question capture, application and source checks

incremental.description: Maintain item-source links and version references

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=14+80=94; gross 6 minus 2 upkeep gives net 4. High assumes repeated source searching; low removes only 2 hours, offset by upkeep. Customer discussion retains all time.

role.altitude: Reduce return entry, carrier lookup and catalogue hunting while retaining physical inspection, compatibility checks and customer advice.
reach: Help counter staff capture reliable equipment and shipment identifiers before technical or carrier decisions
role.ambitious_version: A parts salesperson who brings checked sources and accurate shipment data to customer decisions while retaining responsibility for physical and technical uncertainty.
